chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For Allah there are servants for whom in their loins are wombs like the wombs of women.' He was asked, 'So why do they not bear (children)?' He said: 'They are inverted, and for them in their behinds is a gland like the gland of the camel or the she-camel. So whenever it stirs, they stir, and when it is calm, they are calm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual physiology of the unique servants of Allah described in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual physiology of Allah's special servants, describing their 'wombs' as inverted in their loins and a gland in their backs that governs their spiritual state. This unique anatomy signifies that their inner spiritual condition is not bound by ordinary biological constraints, but rather responds directly to divine will, mirroring the behavior of a camel's hump when it rises or settles. This metaphor highlights the profound connection between their physical form and their spiritual receptivity to God's commands.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdul Rahman Al Azramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are servant for whom in their loins are wombs like the wombs of the women’. So he<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘So what is the matter they are not bearing (children)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are inverted, and for them in their behinds is a gland like the gland of the he-camel, or the she-camel. So whenever it stirs, they stir, and when it is calm, they are calm’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-‘Arzamiy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Of Allah’s creatures there are those who have wombs in their backs like the wombs of women.’ He (the Imam) said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin was asked, ‘Why do not they then become pregnant?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Because it is upside down. In their behind there is a gland like that of camel and when it is excited they become excited and when it is calm they are calm.’”
